Inference cost economics (a token-reseller/relay economy selling ~$0.13 of usage per $1; Recursive Harness Self-Improvement cutting inference cost up to 60%; RAGU at ~$0.001/doc against ~$0.10 for API GraphRAG)

Semiconductor & compute supply chain (Epoch AI: deployed AI chips double every nine months, moving the binding constraint from chip scarcity to energy, capital and permitting; Kimi K3 argued as better performance-per-dollar on MI355X than B300; AMD demonstrates a complete pretraining pipeline on Instinct)

Compute capex & datacentre financing (Anthropic, Macquarie Asset Management and GIC stand up Theseus Infrastructure — the funds own the platform and carry the capex, Anthropic signs long-term leases as anchor tenant and pledges 100% of grid-upgrade costs plus consumer tariff impact; Intel raises $15bn for packaging and foundry; NYT reports the most-polluting US power plant is going up for an Amazon data centre)

Sovereign AI infrastructure (the Swiss public sector enters the hiring file at all three tiers of government in one pass — MeteoSchweiz federal, Kanton Luzern advertising a named 'KI-Plattform-Spezialist', Stadt Bern municipal, plus USZ, ZHdK, ZHAW and HES-SO — nine public reqs from zero in the file's entire prior history, invisible until now because they are posted in German and French as 'KI'; Swisscom launches an in-country Swiss AI Platform; Infomaniak and Omnilex hire for sovereign-cloud and data-residency runtimes)

AI spend & bubble accounting (Torsten Sløk argues AI profits are funded by investors rather than earned from customers with Oracle as exhibit A; a 70%-of-revenue-from-two-labs concentration claim draws more comments than points; HN's second-order read on local models is that "the data center buildout will end in carnage")

Global AI governance blocs (OpenAI petitions a US governor on datacenter siting while an OpenAI strategist argues labs should rival government power; the Commission begins enforcing; Alibaba prepares the first flagship-scale open-weighting; Switzerland runs a national sovereignty agenda around Apertus — four different theories of who sets the rules)

Inference cost economics (DeepSeek warns of "significant" API price rises, blaming capacity not competition, after loss-leader pricing dragged ByteDance and Tencent down with it; GitHub retires Models because coding-agent usage made subsidised token pools unaffordable; OmniRoute's 290-provider arbitrage gateway gains 2,007 stars in three days)

Semiconductor supply chain (Intel raises $15bn in its first public share sale since 1971, earmarked for advanced packaging and foundry capacity — the actual bottleneck behind every accelerator roadmap including NVIDIA's — with the stock up ~175% in 2026; Stoa Markets launches a spot marketplace for GPU and AI-server capacity)

Compute capex & financing (Vantage weighing a ~$100B IPO raising ~$10B, Oracle delaying several OpenAI datacentres by up to a year, SemiAnalysis rebutting the 'half of 2026 capacity cancelled' claim with satellite chiller tracking)

Sovereign & non-US AI infrastructure (L&T's ~$1.57B 10,000-B300 Chennai cluster for Together AI, Naver funding wave-powered offshore compute, Microsoft down to ~1.5% of worldwide revenue in China, Apertus and Swisscom)

Corporate AI mandate & bubble sentiment (Cognition at $40B+, Lovable at $13.3B, a mooted ~$100B Vantage listing, 'my AI agents shipped 128 releases of a product no one ever used', 70% of Americans opposing data centres)

Global AI governance blocs (Microsoft closing at least 15 China branches and JVs as export controls bite, Chinese censorship leaking into American model answers, lab-level divergence across Chinese frontier models, India's largest single-cluster build)

Inference cost economics (Grok 4.6 at $2/$6 against GPT-5.6 Sol's $5/$30, DeepSeek V4 Pro GA at $0.435/$0.87, Anthropic reportedly paying ~$6B for Decart to buy inference efficiency, rtk/caveman/Decant token tooling)
Semiconductor & memory supply chain (Kioxia/Sandisk 2Tb QLC NAND aimed at checkpoint-heavy workloads, 10,000 B300s bound for Chennai, the Rubin CPX roadmap, Stratechery's 'Nvidia's Risky Business')

Compute capex & financing (FT analysis puts accumulated AI purchase commitments at Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, NVIDIA, Oracle and Meta near $1.5T — contractual obligations, not capex, and separate from another ~$1.5T in Goldman-identified leases; Mistral's European Compute Units underwrite ~200 MW by end-2027 off an anchor group of five European buyers)

Global AI governance blocs (Apple registers an on-device generative service with Chinese regulators and builds a China LLM with Alibaba, so fragmentation is now shaping the model layer rather than the compliance layer; DeepSeek's new peak windows map to Chinese working hours — an unintentional disclosure that its traffic is mostly domestic)

Corporate AI mandates & the token-spend question (OpenAI's own adoption paper takes a specific, checkable methodology teardown — undisclosed non-adopter sampling rate, 10-seat pilots counted as adoption, and measured adoption really being measured *sanctioned* adoption; meanwhile German firms budget ~€35M each for 2026 expecting 24% returns, up from 17%)

Semiconductor & compute supply chain (non-NVIDIA inference silicon gets a production seat at a frontier lab — Cerebras wafer-scale with 44 GB on-die SRAM serving GPT-5.6 Sol; SMIC hits 93.7% utilisation with profit more than tripling, and Applied Materials targets a doubling of semiconductor-system output by 2028)
